problem.title: Signal Panel
problem.statement: A signal panel shows one light color and plays one sound. There are 3 light colors and 4 sounds, and every light can be paired with every sound. How many different signals are possible?
hints: A finished signal contains both a light choice and a sound choice.
For each light color, how many sounds can follow?

solutionSteps.title: Define one signal
solutionSteps.body: A complete signal is one light-and-sound pair.

solutionSteps.title: Count continuations
solutionSteps.body: Each of the 3 light colors can be paired with all 4 sounds.

solutionSteps.title: Multiply
solutionSteps.body: The three branches each have four endings, so 3 × 4 = 12 signals.

validationMethods: exhaustive enumeration of the 3-by-4 light-and-sound grid

problem.title: Reading Corner
problem.statement: A reading corner has 4 different comic books and 5 different puzzle books. Lina chooses exactly one book. How many choices does she have?
hints: One chosen book comes from one shelf, not both.
The comic and puzzle books are distinct choices.

solutionSteps.title: Separate the alternatives
solutionSteps.body: A chosen book is either one of the 4 comics or one of the 5 puzzle books.

solutionSteps.title: Check the cases
solutionSteps.body: The cases cover every allowed choice and share no book.

validationMethods: direct enumeration of four comic titles and five puzzle titles
notes: Recomputed answer: 4 + 5 = 9; the two shelves are disjoint.

problem.title: Ice Cream Cones
problem.statement: An ice cream cone has one flavor and one topping. There are 4 flavors and 3 toppings, and every topping is available with every flavor. How many different cones are possible?
hints: A finished cone is a flavor-topping pair.
For each flavor, count all three topping choices.

solutionSteps.title: Define one outcome
solutionSteps.body: Every complete cone contains one flavor and one topping.

solutionSteps.title: Count the branches
solutionSteps.body: Each of 4 flavors has 3 topping continuations.

validationMethods: exhaustive enumeration of the 4-by-3 flavor-and-topping grid

problem.title: Island Ferries
problem.statement: To reach an island, a traveler chooses one ferry and one of that ferry's departure times. Harbor Ferry leaves at 8:00, 10:00, and 1:00. Bay Ferry leaves at 9:00 and 12:00. How many different ferry-and-time plans are possible?
hints: The two ferry branches have different numbers of endings.
Count the complete Harbor plans and complete Bay plans.

solutionSteps.title: Join the ferry cases
solutionSteps.body: A plan uses exactly one ferry, so 3 + 2 = 5 plans.

validationMethods: explicit enumeration of the five named ferry-and-time plans
notes: Recomputed answer: 3 Harbor plans + 2 Bay plans = 5.

problem.title: Symbol Tiles
problem.statement: A tile shows one symbol and has one border color. The symbol is one of the letters A, B, C or one of the digits 1, 2. The border is black or white. How many different tiles are possible?
hints: How many total symbol choices are there?
Each symbol can receive either border color.

solutionSteps.title: Count symbols
solutionSteps.body: The 3 letters and 2 digits are disjoint symbol choices, giving 3 + 2 = 5 symbols.

solutionSteps.title: Add the second stage
solutionSteps.body: Each symbol pairs with either of 2 border colors.

validationMethods: exhaustive enumeration of five symbols crossed with two borders
notes: Recomputed answer: (3 + 2) × 2 = 10; independently, 6 letter tiles + 4 digit tiles = 10.

problem.title: One Festival Event
problem.statement: A student chooses exactly one festival event. In the morning, each of 2 workshops is offered in any of 3 rooms. In the afternoon, each of 3 talks is offered in either of 2 rooms. How many workshop-or-talk event choices are possible?
hints: Count complete morning events and complete afternoon events separately.
A chosen event cannot be both morning and afternoon.

solutionSteps.title: Count morning events
solutionSteps.body: Two workshops paired with three rooms give 2 × 3 = 6 morning events.

solutionSteps.title: Count afternoon events
solutionSteps.body: Three talks paired with two rooms give 3 × 2 = 6 afternoon events.

solutionSteps.title: Join the time blocks
solutionSteps.body: Morning and afternoon are disjoint cases, so 6 + 6 = 12 events.

validationMethods: exhaustive two-block enumeration of six morning and six afternoon events
notes: Recomputed answer: 2 × 3 + 3 × 2 = 12; the time blocks are disjoint.
